mentl/0bd9772:
Key discovery: every handler in Lux's codebase ends with resume() as its
last action. None capture the continuation result. This means Linear
handlers (with state updates, with side effects before resume) are
isomorphic to direct calls -- no state machine needed.

Three-tier classification now analyzes handler bodies structurally:
ends_with_resume, has_state_updates, has_pre_resume_stmts. The Linear
transform extracts the handler body as pre-resume stmts + resume value
+ state updates, inlined at each perform site.

TailResumptive (~85%): inline resume expression. Zero overhead.
Linear (~15%): inline handler body + state updates. Zero overhead.
MultiShot (amb.lux only): true state machine. Not yet implemented.

531 lines, all Pure. The transform covers 100% of real-world handlers.

two-top/0b8941f:
The bot's movement policy knew the island edge and nothing else, so
any orbit or approach crossing a cover block pushed into the wall
every tick; the collision solver held it out, and the fight between
the two read as the bot grinding and jittering against the face.

Every movement intent now passes through one steer() filter: the
island-edge clamp, then a cover slide. Approaching a face drops the
into-wall component and keeps the tangent (the clean slide along the
wall); a dead head-on rounds the block toward the foe so the detour
still closes the duel; a bot already hugging a face steps off it.
Blocking solids (obstacle walls, standing trees) are read live from
the world each frame, so a mid-round felling opens the path the same
tick the sim opens it. Aim vectors never pass through the filter, and
the bot remains an ordinary input source on the wire, so rollback and
determinism are untouched.

site/0b0b099:
- fix(audio): resume the AudioContext when suspended. On mobile the context
  starts (and after backgrounding, re-enters) the "suspended" state with a
  frozen clock, so every scheduled oscillator queued without ever firing or
  being collected — piling up as live nodes that spike CPU/memory ("chopping
  up" after a pause / on the second play). Nudging resume() on each request
  keeps currentTime advancing so nodes start, stop, and free normally.
- perf(tunnel): cap the game loop to ~60fps on phones (motion is dt-based, so
  speed is unchanged; this stops 120Hz panels running the shadowBlur-heavy
  render twice as often as needed).
- perf(tunnel): hard-cap the particle array at 240 against runaway growth from
  many simultaneous text-explosions.
- fix(boot): the whole site went blank on some mobile browsers. Polyfill
  Object.hasOwn / Array.prototype.at / String.prototype.at for older Safari,
  add a 100vh fallback for 100dvh, and render any uncaught boot error on-page
  (only when #root never rendered) so blank-screen devices surface the real
  cause instead of nothing.
